artifacts.description: feat(io): build and load body BReps and the display mesh

acceptance_criteria: `pub const DISPLAY_DEFLECTION_MM: f64 = 0.05`, `pub fn build_part_cache<K: Kernel>(kernel: &K, doc: &mut Document, bodies: &[(String, &K::Shape)], deflection_mm: f64) -> Result<(), …>` and `pub fn load_body<K: Kernel>(kernel: &K, doc: &Document, body_id: &str) -> Option<K::Shape>`, documented, as in spec §3. Every entry built gets the document's current `model_hash`.

With `--features occt`: a 40 × 25 × 10 mm box as body `b-1` gives `cache/body-b-1.brep` and `cache/display.glb`. Written and read back through both the unpacked and the `.sltwx` form, `load_body` returns a shape whose volume is 10 000 mm³ within 1e-9 relative, and the GLB's position accessor min/max equal the box corners within 1e-4 mm.
With `--features occt`: a `.brep` entry whose bytes are replaced by `garbage` (with its `sha256` updated to match) makes `load_body` return `None`, with no panic.
With `--features occt`: stale after edit (spec §6): build the cache, change one parameter expression in `model`, and `load_body` returns `None`.
An invalid `deflection_mm` (not finite, or ≤ 0) returns an error before any tessellation and leaves `doc.cache` unchanged.

`cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test --workspace` pass, and `cargo clippy -p swx-io --features occt --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo test -p swx-io --features occt` pass (CI does not run the `swx-io` occt tests; report the local run).
QA report (FACTORY §6b) posted on the PR.
